chunks: Al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about the salat of the eclipse, the eclipse of the sun and the moon. He said:

“It is ten rakʿahs and four sajdahs. You perform rukuʿ five times, then perform sajdah in the fifth; then you perform rukuʿ five times, then perform sajdah in the tenth. If you wish, you may recite a surah in each rakʿah, and if you wish, you may recite half a surah in each rakʿah. فإذا recite a surah in each rakʿah, then recite Fātiḥat al-Kitāb; and if you recite half a surah, it suffices for you not to recite Fātiḥat al-Kitāb except in the first rakʿah until you begin another one. And do not say, ‘Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah,’ when raising your head from rukuʿ except in the rakʿah in which you intend to perform sajdah.”

key_terms.الْخَامِسَةِ: the fifth bowing, after which sajdah is performed
key_terms.الْعَاشِرَةِ: the tenth bowing, after which sajdah is performed
key_terms.رَكَعَاتٍ: units or cycles of the prayer in this ritual form
key_terms.سَجَدَاتٍ: the prostrations included in the prayer
key_terms.سُورَةً: a chapter of the Qur'an recited in the prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْكُسُوفِ: the eclipse prayer performed for solar and lunar eclipses
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, the opening chapter recited in salat

ai.seo_question: How is salat al-kusuf performed according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of performing salat al-kusuf for solar and lunar eclipses. It outlines the number of rakʿahs, rukuʿs, and sajdahs, and clarifies the recitation pattern of surahs and Fātiḥat al-Kitāb during the prayer. It also specifies when the phrase ‘Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah’ is to be said.
